ev.quote: Aidan N. Gomez∗ † University of Toronto aidan@cs.toronto.edu
31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.

contribution.value: Introduces the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture based solely on self-attention, removing recurrence and convolutions and enabling far more parallel training while reaching state-of-the-art translation quality.

ev.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
We trained on the standard WMT 2014 English-German dataset consisting of about 4.5 million sentence pairs.
For English-French, we used the significantly larger WMT 2014 English-French dataset consisting of 36M sentences
We trained a 4-layer transformer with dmodel = 1024 on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) portion of the Penn Treebank
we also trained it in a semi-supervised setting, using the larger high-confidence and BerkleyParser corpora from with approximately 17M sentences

data_size.value: WMT En-De ~4.5M sentence pairs (37K BPE vocab); WMT En-Fr 36M sentences (32K word-piece vocab); WSJ ~40K training sentences for parsing

ev.quote: We trained on the standard WMT 2014 English-German dataset consisting of about 4.5 million sentence pairs.

models_used.value: Transformer (base): N=6, d_model=512, d_ff=2048, h=8, ~65M params
Transformer (big): N=6, d_model=1024, d_ff=4096, h=16, ~213M params
Transformer (4 layers) for constituency parsing, d_model=1024

ev.quote: We trained a 4-layer transformer with dmodel = 1024 on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) portion of the Penn Treebank
Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 Englishto-German translation task
Listed perplexities are per-wordpiece, according to our byte-pair encoding, and should not be compared to per-word perplexities.

key_results.value: Transformer (big) reaches 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 EN-DE, beating prior best (including ensembles) by over 2 BLEU

ev.quote: Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 Englishto-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU.

key_results.value: Transformer (big) reaches 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 EN-FR, a new single-model state of the art, after 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs

ev.quote: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs

key_results.value: Transformer (base) reaches 27.3 BLEU EN-DE / 38.1 BLEU EN-FR at training cost 3.3×10^18 FLOPs, far below prior models
4-layer Transformer reaches 91.3 F1 on WSJ-23 (WSJ-only) and 92.7 F1 (semi-supervised), outperforming most prior parsers

ev.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.
We trained our models on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.
Even our base model surpasses all previously published models and ensembles, at a fraction of the training cost of any of the competitive models.

strengths.value: Removes recurrence and convolutions, allowing far more parallel training and shorter wall-clock time to state of the art.

ev.quote: The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.

strengths.value: Sets a new single-model state of the art on WMT 2014 EN-DE (28.4 BLEU) and EN-FR (41.8 BLEU).

ev.quote: Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 Englishto-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU.

strengths.value: Self-attention gives O(1) maximum path length between any two positions, easing long-range dependency learning.

ev.quote: As noted in Table 1, a self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations.

strengths.value: Generalises beyond translation: a 4-layer Transformer reaches 92.7 F1 on WSJ constituency parsing with little tuning.

ev.quote: Our results in Table 4 show that despite the lack of task-specific tuning our model performs surprisingly well

weaknesses.value: Self-attention costs O(n^2 · d) per layer, becoming expensive for very long sequences relative to recurrent layers.

ev.quote: To improve computational performance for tasks involving very long sequences, self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of size r in the input sequence

weaknesses.value: Multi-head attention has reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions, only partly fixed by multiple heads.

ev.quote: albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention

weaknesses.value: Reducing attention key size d_k hurts quality, suggesting dot-product compatibility may be insufficient.

ev.quote: we observe that reducing the attention key size d^(k) hurts model quality. This suggests that determining compatibility is not easy and that a more sophisticated compatibility function than dot product may be beneficial.

weaknesses.value: Single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting; quality also drops with too many heads.

ev.quote: While single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting, quality also drops off with too many heads.

limitations.value: Evaluated only on machine translation and English constituency parsing, not on other modalities such as image, audio or video.

ev.quote: We plan to extend the Transformer to problems involving input and output modalities other than text and to investigate local, restricted attention mechanisms

limitations.value: Generation remains sequential at inference time and the paper flags this as an open problem.

ev.quote: Making generation less sequential is another research goals of ours.

limitations.value: No quantization, pruning or compression study — all results use full-precision (FP32/FP16) parameters.
No edge or low-power deployment evaluation; training and inference are reported only on data-centre P100 GPUs.

ev.quote: We trained our models on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

future_work_stated.value: Apply attention-based models to non-text modalities such as images, audio and video.

ev.quote: We plan to extend the Transformer to problems involving input and output modalities other than text

future_work_stated.value: Investigate local, restricted attention to handle very large inputs and outputs efficiently.

ev.quote: to investigate local, restricted attention mechanisms to efficiently handle large inputs and outputs such as images, audio and video

future_work_stated.value: Make sequence generation less sequential at inference time.

ev.quote: Making generation less sequential is another research goals of ours.

future_work_stated.value: Explore restricted self-attention with neighborhood size r for very long sequences.

ev.quote: self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of size r in the input sequence centered around the respective output position. This would increase the maximum path length to O(n/r). We plan to investigate this approach further in future work.
